newsitem.title: UK: Europe, Asia LPG prices hold firm despite weak US.
newsitem.headline: Europe, Asia LPG prices hold firm despite weak US.

text.p: Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices in Europe and Asia shrugged off a sluggish U.S. market and headed higher this week, with the propane market particularly well-supported by a freezein Europe, traders said.
In Europe, the small sea-going propane coaster market made strong gains, with a parcel traded into the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp region on Friday at a buoyant $382.50 a tonne.

Traders said that Arctic conditions across northwest Europe were helping to keep the heat under prices. "I think the market looked fundamentally strong anyway, and now we're seeing this colder weather, it's getting another boost," said one trader.
No deals were reported on larger cargoes with most traders absent from the market due to the holidays. But prices were assessed notionally steady to firmer in the mid $360s cif ARA.
The tone of the thinly-discussed butane market was softer, traders said.
"There's much less buying interest for butane," said one. "There are a lot of sellers and perhaps a distressed cargo or two on the water."
In the Middle East, state-owned Saudi Aramco awarded both propane and butane at around $335 a tonne in its second January tender, the T2 tender, Japanese buyers said.
